additionalCoursework:
The University of Michigan Medical School (UMMS) recognizes that the field of medicine offers opportunities for those talented in both humanities and the sciences. Therefore, students should allow their personal interests and passion to dictate their choice of undergraduate major or subsequent area(s) of study. We do not require or prescribe any specific coursework for admission to UMMS. However, the UMMS curriculum has been designed with the presumption that our admitted students possess a foundational level of knowledge and skills upon which to build further competency in medical knowledge, communication and other domains necessary to become excellent physicians.

The listed competencies that we require of matriculants to UMMS fall under the following categories:

-Humanities & Social Sciences (including skills in Written and Verbal Communication)
-Life and Physical Sciences
-Statistics
-Analytical Thinking and Problem-Solving Skills

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
UMMS is committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive learning environment for all students. We work with qualified candidates who may require specific accommodations on a case-by-case basis to ensure our technical standards can be reasonably met. We also encourage students with Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) to apply to our MD program.

medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities:
Students are encouraged to explore personal interests outside of medical school, and with more than 100 medical student-specific groups, there is no shortage of opportunities to get involved. Ranging from socially and academically focused to service and identity oriented, these groups help students learn, create meaningful change and connect with their community – and the community at large. 

The M-Home Learning community not only serves as students' academic and professional base but also provides numerous opportunities for informal and formal social activities that bring members of all the classes together. 

Through M-Home and the MM Office of Well-Being, medical students have access to a full range of wellbeing and mental health resources, including free psychological and psychiatric services, and formal peer support programs.

Student Orgs: https://medschool.umich.edu/student-organizations
M-Home: https://michmed.org/xNxR3
Health & Well-Being: https://michmed.org/WXVGD
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The University of Michigan Medical School is situated within walking distance of the University's main campus and downtown Ann Arbor. 

Located along the banks of the Huron River, the city offers a compact urban experience and recreational activities that appeal to students, professionals, singles & families. It is a diverse and culturally rich community that attracts visitors and residents from all over the world.

Ann Arbor is home to 150+ parks, the Nichols Arboretum, and miles of walking/biking paths. Foodies enjoy 300+ restaurants, and world-renown artists perform in the city's many venues. Some medical students purchase tickets as a group to cheer on the Wolverines in sporting events like football, hockey, basketball, or join an intramural team like soccer. 

Ann Arbor is a short drive from Detroit and its international airport, and a 4-hour drive from Chicago and Toronto and the beautiful scenery of northern Michigan. 
 
https://medschool.umich.edu/our-community/about-ann-arbor
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Ann Arbor offers a wide range of safe and affordable housing for students. Most medical students choose to live in apartments within walking distance of the medical campus.  Free public transportation opens up many more options, including on- and off-campus housing and two active medical society chapters where some students live.

https://medschool.umich.edu/our-community/housing

medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Here you’ll find a world-class public university ready to welcome you from the moment you arrive on campus. Medical students form a close-knit community, supporting one another in the learning environment and through social connections and activities. Your peers are here to help you study, to offer advice and to teach you fun traditions when you become a Michigan Wolverine. 

Our expert faculty and staff are here to guide you, offering mentorship that will foster your professional and personal growth. We provide you with a supportive and collaborative setting to spark learning and innovation while our commitment to diversity creates an inclusive environment where all backgrounds are valued and respected. 

You’ll find that our culture offers you a balanced quality of life and the flexibility to pursue your passions – all within an academically rigorous environment that’s dedicated to shaping you into an empathetic and skilled physician. 

Community: https://michmed.org/bwMXP

medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Advancing patient care through biomedical research since 1850, the University of Michigan counts the first synthetic penicillin breakthrough, introduction of the electrocardiogram, and creation of the first human genetics program among its many contributions. 
 
A top-ranked research school, UMMS devotes key resources to funding, facilities and faculty mentorship for students who are interested in basic, clinical, translational and outcomes research both on campus and abroad. 

It’s easy for students to do research at Michigan, especially through individualized experiences in the Branches phase of the curriculum. More information: https://medschool.umich.edu/programs-admissions/md-program/md-program-opportunities/md-program-opportunities-research

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The University of Michigan Medical School is committed to providing a welcoming and inclusive learning environment for all students who are training to care for an increasingly diverse and complex patient population. The school has a long, distinguished history as part of the world-renowned University of Michigan, which is home to many highly ranked professional schools. This allows our students myriad options to pursue research, dual degrees and other collaborations. 

The school is also part of Michigan Medicine, a large academic medical center with consistently high clinical rankings. Students have exposure to urban and rural patient populations through programs with other hospitals, medical groups and agencies. Students may also choose to rotate at other U.S. hospitals or abroad. Our comprehensive clinical training is also highly customizable, and graduates are well prepared for residency and typically have higher-than-average match rates.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
To transform health through bold and innovative education, discovery and service. Strategic pillars for the school are focused on people, discovery, education, care and service.
•	People: recruit, develop and retain the best faculty, staff and learners who work together for the greater good.
•	Discovery: create transformative knowledge that advances science and improves health.
•	Education: cultivate a learning community that engages all in bold and innovative education for the advancement of science, health and health care delivery.
•	Care: deliver outstanding patient care and improve health for local, national and global populations while caring for each other.
•	Service: engage and collaborate with our institutional, local, state, national and global communities to advance health and science.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
The University of Michigan Medical School will look positively upon individuals who have discovered personal areas of academic interest through their curricular and extracurricular activities, and have worked to independently develop, refine and distinguish their experiences to improve and advance health care. 

Since the many fields of medicine offer opportunities for those talented in both humanities and the sciences, students should allow personal interests and their passion to dictate their choice of an undergraduate major. 

Students should view prerequisites as competencies to develop and not as specific course requirements.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: There is no expiration date on prerequisite coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
All applicants to the University of Michigan Medical School are expected to demonstrate a strong foundation of knowledge across core scientific subjects as well as the inter/intrapersonal skills needed by physicians to thrive in an ever-changing health care landscape. 
The Admissions Committee is committed to individually assessing each applicant's potential as a physician.  Information used in the assessment includes the application, letters of recommendation, personal statements, coursework, interviews and personal communication from those acquainted with the individual.  Each applicant will be assessed on essential skills, intelligence, and personal attributes (academic excellence, cultural humility, dedication to medicine, altruism, integrity and communication skills) and on their unique potential to contribute to the educational experience at Michigan and to the profession of medicine.

https://medschool.umich.edu/programs-admissions/md-program/md-admissions/md-admissions-faqs
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: UMMS does not have a shadowing requirement. We prefer that candidates get quality, active exposure in the field of medicine or related fields.
